terms.proofCondition: Settled cash received totals the target within the window

strategy.title: No plan yet: the number of clinics that would buy is only an estimate
strategy.why: The offer is otherwise sound: $260 per monthly packet (three October invoices), 3 of 20 contacts accepted, $4 cost, no capital, Brain produces the spreadsheet, cash in 6 days. But $3,500 needs 14 packets at $256 net, i.e. 14 distinct clinics buying once in the 30-day monthly cycle, and at 3/20 that means ~94 reachable clinic managers. The only count of clinics is a RECOMMENDATION ('probably number in the dozens'), an estimate that cannot establish the market; if 'dozens' is literal, ~3-7 deals is all the market yields.

alternatives.title: Start outreach now and treat it as a conditional test
alternatives.why: The conversion rate is already measured; what is unknown is how many buyers exist, which a directory count answers faster and without spending outreach on a market that may be too small.

facts.value: Independent sleep clinics in the region probably number in the dozens and would each need these packets monthly.
Sell Monthly CPAP adherence-report packets for payer re-authorisation at sleep-medicine clinics to each buyer.
Invoices (Oct 2026): three clinics each paid $260 for a monthly adherence-report batch.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN naming MARKET_VOLUME as the decisive gap is correct. The price ($260, three October invoices actually paid by clinics), conversion (3/20 on this offer), cost ($4), exposure ($0), fulfilment (Brain spreadsheet) and settlement (6 days) are on the card as EVIDENCE, but the only buyer count is a RECOMMENDATION ('probably number in the dozens'), which is an estimate and cannot establish volume. Arithmetic checks: $3,500 / $260 = 13.5, so 14 packets; at 15% that needs ~94 reachable clinics; if 'dozens' means 24-84, the market yields ~4-13 new deals, which may fall short, so the count really does decide the outcome. This is missing evidence, not a constraint, and the plan correctly does not call it one. The resolution (count from a published directory such as the AASM accredited-facility directory; re-plan at >= ~94) is zero-cost and decisive; Brain's own reading names the same gap.
findings: Existing customers: the three October clinics bought a monthly batch, so on the card's own 'monthly' statement they are repeat buyers within the window (3 x $260 = $780), reducing the new clinics needed to ~11 (~74 contacts at 15%). The re-plan should count them, if their renewal is recorded.
Small sample: 3/20 has a wide interval (a 95% lower bound near 3-5%); the re-plan should show the target still holds if conversion is well below 15%, or carry a stop rule on the measured rate.
Card records 1 human hour per packet; no hours ceiling, so it fits, but the re-plan should state it.
